introduction_markdown:
**General Certificate of Education Board - General Certificate of Education Examination. Physics 2 (0780), ADVANCED LEVEL, June 2024. Time allowed: three hours.**

Answer ALL questions. Section I is designed to be answered in 1 hour, Section II in 30 minutes and Section III in 1 hour. You are advised to divide your time accordingly. You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers. In calculations you must show all the steps in your working, giving your answer at each stage. Calculators and formulae booklet are allowed.

**Structure of the paper.** SECTION I (One hour): questions 1 to 5 are compulsory; in question 6 answer EITHER 6 (a), (b) and (c) OR 6 (d), (e) and (f). SECTION II (30 minutes): DATA ANALYSIS, question 7. SECTION III (1 hour): OPTIONS - answer any two questions from the four options (Option 1: Energy resources and environmental physics, question 8; Option 2: Communication, question 9; Option 3: Electronics, question 10; Option 4: Medical physics, question 11).

No data sheet is printed in the paper: whenever a constant is needed, the model answer states the value it uses.

questions.enonce_markdown:
Figure 11 shows the block diagram of an *amplitude modulation* (AM) radio receiver (the phrase *amplitude modulation* is underlined in the paper).

![fig-1](gce-al-physics-2024-p2-officiel-cameroun_exercice_9_fig_1.png)

(i) Explain the meaning of the underlined phrase.

(ii) Copy and complete the above block diagram.

(iii) State the functions of the tuned circuit and the demodulator.
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i) Amplitude modulation.** The sound (audio-frequency) signal to be sent is used to vary the **amplitude** of a high-frequency carrier wave: the amplitude of the carrier changes in step with the instantaneous value of the audio signal, while the frequency of the carrier stays constant. The envelope of the modulated carrier has the shape of the audio signal.

**(ii) Completed block diagram.** In order, joined by arrows, from the aerial to the loudspeaker:

Aerial $\rightarrow$ **tuned circuit** $\rightarrow$ **radio-frequency (RF) amplifier** $\rightarrow$ **demodulator** $\rightarrow$ **audio-frequency (AF) amplifier** $\rightarrow$ **loudspeaker.**

The first empty box (between the tuned circuit and the demodulator) is the RF amplifier and the second (between the demodulator and the loudspeaker) is the AF amplifier.

**(iii) Functions.**

- **Tuned circuit:** it selects the wanted station. The $LC$ circuit is adjusted (tuned) to resonate at the carrier frequency of the station, so it accepts signals of that frequency and rejects signals of all other frequencies picked up by the aerial.
- **Demodulator (detector):** it separates the audio-frequency signal from the carrier. It rectifies the modulated signal and smooths it, removing the high-frequency carrier, so that only the audio signal passes on to the AF amplifier.

questions.enonce_markdown:
(i) Why is the mobile phone referred to as a transceiver?

(ii) Bring out two differences between a mobile telephone handset and a commercial radio transmitter like that of CRTV with respect to telecommunication.

(iii) State one environmental problem which is related to the use of mobile phones.
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i)** A mobile phone contains both a **trans**mitter and a re**ceiver**: it sends signals (your voice) and receives signals (the other person's voice) with the same device, which is why it is called a transceiver.

**(ii)** Any two of:

| Mobile telephone handset | Commercial radio transmitter (e.g. CRTV) |
|---|---|
| Two-way (duplex): it transmits and receives at the same time. | One-way: it only transmits (broadcasts); listeners only receive. |
| Low transmitting power (a fraction of a watt to about $2\ \mathrm{W}$) and short range: it talks to the nearest base station of the cell. | High power (kilowatts) and a large range: it covers a whole region from one tall mast. |
| Point-to-point: the call is addressed to one particular receiver (the number dialled). | Broadcast: the signal goes to every receiver in range tuned to the station. |

**(iii)** Any one of: electronic waste (discarded handsets and batteries contain toxic metals such as lead, cadmium and mercury); the electromagnetic radiation and the visual and land pollution caused by base-station masts; the use of energy to charge phones.

questions.enonce_markdown:
Signals transmitted through optical fibres suffer less attenuation than those transmitted through copper cables. Signal attenuation, measured in decibels (dB), is given by:

$$\text{Attenuation} = 10\log\left(\frac{P_{\mathrm{in}}}{P_{\mathrm{out}}}\right)$$

(i) State two other advantages of optical fibres over copper cables in telecommunication.

(ii) A typical multimode optical fibre has an attenuation per unit length of $0.90\ \mathrm{dB\,km^{-1}}$. What will be the power of a $4.0\ \mathrm{mW}$ signal over a distance of $12\ \mathrm{km}$?
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i)** Any two of:

- a very large bandwidth: far more information (many more telephone channels or television channels) can be carried by one fibre;
- no interference from electric and magnetic fields (no pick-up of noise, and no cross-talk between neighbouring fibres);
- greater security: the signal is difficult to tap without being noticed;
- the fibre is thinner, lighter, cheaper (glass compared with copper) and does not corrode.

**(ii) Power received.** Total attenuation over $12\ \mathrm{km}$:
$$0.90\ \mathrm{dB\,km^{-1}}\times12\ \mathrm{km} = 10.8\ \mathrm{dB}.$$
With $P_{\mathrm{in}} = 4.0\ \mathrm{mW}$:
$$10\log\left(\frac{P_{\mathrm{in}}}{P_{\mathrm{out}}}\right) = 10.8\quad\Rightarrow\quad\frac{P_{\mathrm{in}}}{P_{\mathrm{out}}} = 10^{1.08} = 12.0.$$
$$P_{\mathrm{out}} = \frac{4.0}{12.0} = 0.33\ \mathrm{mW}.$$
**The signal power after $12\ \mathrm{km}$ is about $0.33\ \mathrm{mW}$.**
